paper_metadata.title: Study of the Tensile and Fatigue Properties of Quinary Strengthening Phase in Ni-Based Superalloys

evidence.quote: Ni-based superalloys are extensively utilized as the primary mate-rial for turbine blades in aircraft and power generation turbines, due to their exceptional high-temperature creep resistance, fatigue strength, and corrosion resistance.
In this work, a Ni– Al– Co– Cr– Ti quinary embedded atom method (EAM) potential was developed speciﬁcally for the DZ411 alloy.

At elevated temperatures above 1100 K, the dislocation density decreases, primarily due to dislocation climb, leading to a gradual transformation of the crystal structure from FCC to HCP.
The results show that the alloy forms HCP structures in the γ matrix during room-temperature tensile process.
the strengthening element Ti promotes the formation of BCC structures in the γ 0 phase, which is used to ensure the stability of the alloy at high temperatures.

When the alloy reaches its UTS (strain rate of 10%), the dislocation density within the alloy peaks. A large variety of dislocations concentrate at the phase interfaces, and some also appear within the bulk of the alloy.
As the applied stress gradually increases (strain rate of 4%), the dislocation loops within the alloy begin to break down, and an increasing number of green Shockley dislocations appear.
